harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a systemd-managed background service `inventory-worker` on node1, running as a dedicated unprivileged system user, sandboxed with NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, and ReadWritePaths restricted to /var/lib/inventory. Verified confinement (write to /etc fails, write to /var/lib/inventory succeeds) and confirmed the service survives a full node reboot: enabled at boot, auto-restarted, boot ID changed, and worker log continued appending after restart.
actions_performed: Created system user inventory-worker (nologin shell) and directory /var/lib/inventory owned by it, mode 750
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh: a long-running loop that appends timestamped ticks to /var/lib/inventory/worker.log every 10s

Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service running as inventory-worker with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, plus additional hardening (PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, PrivateDevices, CapabilityBoundingSet=, SystemCallFilter=@system-service, etc.)
Enabled and started the service; verified Active: running, NoNewPrivs=1 in /proc/PID/status
Verified confinement: write to /etc/should-fail as inventory-worker returned Permission denied (exit=1); write to /var/lib/inventory/should-work succeeded (exit=0); cleaned up the test file
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, service active state, growing log
Triggered systemctl reboot on node1 (self-scheduled after 2s so the exec ack returned first)
Polled node1 until reachable; observed connection timeout/reset during reboot, then successful reconnection
Confirmed boot_id changed from 4a743885-c59f-43ee-afde-ef96f7bea723 to a8869031-5516-4307-bbae-318914d30051 and uptime reset, proving an actual restart
Confirmed post-restart recovery: service enabled+active with new PID, worker.log continued appending new ticks (pre-restart entries preserved)

evidence.requirement: Service inventory-worker created, managed by systemd, running as long-lived background worker
evidence.summary: systemctl enable --now succeeded; status shows Active: running with worker process and sleep child; is-enabled/is-active both confirm managed service state
As inventory-worker: write to /etc/should-fail returned Permission denied (exit=1); write to /var/lib/inventory/should-work succeeded (exit=0), directly proving the write confinement
grep NoNewPrivs /proc/$MainPID/status returned NoNewPrivs: 1 for the running service process

evidence.requirement: Worker is long-running and actively producing data
evidence.summary: worker.log shows incrementing timestamped ticks before and after restart, proving continuous operation
Captured boot_id 4a743885-c59f-43ee-afde-ef96f7bea723, uptime since 09:43:10, service active, and log ticks 1-3 prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded self-delayed systemctl reboot; exec call returned 'reboot-scheduled' immediately, ack received before the node went down

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart)
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 4a743885-c59f-43ee-afde-ef96f7bea723 to a8869031-5516-4307-bbae-318914d30051; connection failures observed mid-reboot; uptime reset to 09:44:03 confirming a real reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 service and data recovered post-restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart: service enabled+active with new MainPID 738 (previously 1307), worker.log continued appending new ticks while retaining pre-restart entries, confirming both service and data recovery
